result.text:
This policy explains the warranty support available for eligible Halvard Home purchases used in a private household. It is for customers who have bought directly from Halvard Home or through an authorised retailer and want to understand their cover, request help or make a claim.

The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship under normal domestic use, subject to the terms set out in this policy. It explains how we assess claims and when we may offer a repair, replacement or alternative remedy.

The policy also describes what is not covered, including accidental damage, misuse, unauthorised alterations and ordinary wear and tear. It sets out your responsibilities for care and maintenance, the information we may need to support a claim and how to contact us.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer and does not limit or replace them.

Register a new appliance within 25 days of delivery to activate the standard warranty. Registration helps Halvard Home link your appliance to your purchase details and check your cover if you need support. It also helps us contact you about important safety information relating to your appliance.

You can register through the warranty registration page on our website or ask our customer support team for help. Please use the contact details published on our website. You do not need to agree to receive marketing messages to register your appliance or activate your standard warranty.

Have your proof of purchase and delivery details ready when you register. We will also ask for your contact information and the appliance details shown on its rating label. Please copy these details carefully so that we can identify your appliance and record your registration correctly.

Your proof of purchase should clearly show the retailer, the appliance purchased and the purchase date. If the delivery date is different, please keep evidence of delivery as well. An order confirmation, receipt or delivery note may help us check the information you provide.

Keep your proof of purchase for at least 64 months after delivery. Store it somewhere safe and make sure any digital copy remains clear and readable. Registration does not replace your proof of purchase, and we may ask to see it when assessing a warranty claim.

Please check your registration confirmation and tell us if anything is wrong. If you do not receive confirmation, contact customer support so that we can check whether your registration has been received. Sending a registration request does not confirm that the details have been accepted.

If you cannot complete registration because information is missing, the website is unavailable or you need an accessible alternative, please contact us for assistance. Explain the difficulty and provide whatever purchase and delivery evidence you have. We will explain what is needed to complete your registration.

If you have missed the registration deadline, contact customer support to discuss your circumstances. We will review the information you provide and explain whether the standard warranty can be activated. Please do not assume that an incomplete or late registration has activated your cover.

Registering an appliance does not change the scope of the warranty. Any claim remains subject to the applicable warranty terms, including the conditions and exclusions described elsewhere in this policy. Please keep your registration confirmation with your purchase records so that they are easy to find.

We use registration information to administer warranty cover, provide support and communicate relevant safety notices. Our privacy notice explains how we handle personal information and how you can exercise your data protection rights. Please let us know if your contact details change.

The registration requirement applies to Halvard Home’s standard warranty. It does not affect your statutory rights, including any rights you may have against the retailer. You do not have to register with us to exercise those rights.

If you believe you have a fault covered by your Halvard Home warranty, contact our customer support team by phone or through the contact options on our website. Explain what has happened and tell us that you wish to make a warranty claim.

Please provide your name, contact details and delivery address, together with a description of the item and the fault. Tell us where you bought it and provide proof of purchase. Clear photographs may help us understand the problem, but please do not put yourself at risk to take them.

Proof of purchase can include a receipt, an order confirmation or other evidence showing where and when you bought the item. If you cannot find this, contact us to discuss what alternative evidence we can accept. You do not need to keep the original packaging to make a claim.

Halvard Home replies to a warranty claim within 18 working days of receiving it. Our reply will explain whether we can assess your claim using the information provided or whether we need further details. It will also explain what you should do next.

A claim made by phone is logged within 58 hours. Please tell our adviser if you need us to contact you in a particular way or if you need support with the claims process.

Describe the fault as clearly as you can, including the circumstances in which it happens. Let us know about any damage, alterations or repairs that may be relevant. Giving us accurate information helps us assess your claim fairly and choose an appropriate way to investigate it.

If you suspect that the item is unsafe, stop using it and contact us for advice. Do not attempt a repair or dismantle it to investigate the fault. Follow the safety instructions supplied with it, where doing so is safe.

We may ask to inspect the item or arrange for it to be collected. Please wait for our instructions before sending anything to us. We will explain how to prepare it for transport and what to include. Tell us if you cannot safely move or package it.

We will assess your claim against the warranty terms and explain our decision in plain language. If the fault is covered, we will tell you what remedy is available and how it will be arranged. We will discuss any practical arrangements with you before proceeding.

If we decide that your claim is not covered, we will explain why and identify the relevant warranty terms. You can ask us to review the decision and provide further evidence. If you remain unhappy, you can use our complaints process.

Making a warranty claim does not affect your statutory rights. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the item, separately from this warranty.

cell.item: POL-WAR/General terms/What the warranty does not cover

result.text:
The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship. It does not cover damage or faults caused by misuse, neglect, accidental damage or use that does not follow the instructions supplied by Halvard Home. We will consider the cause of the fault when assessing a claim.

Damage caused by incorrect installation is not covered. This includes unsuitable connections, inadequate ventilation or placement where the surrounding conditions do not meet the installation instructions. This exclusion does not apply where Halvard Home is responsible for the installation error.

The warranty does not cover faults caused by an unsuitable electricity supply, damaged household wiring or problems with plumbing or drainage outside the appliance. Damage caused by fire, flooding, lightning, pests or other external events is also excluded unless the underlying cause is a fault covered by the warranty.

You are responsible for routine cleaning and care in line with the supplied instructions. The warranty does not cover damage caused by a failure to carry out that care, including damage from blocked openings, accumulated dirt or unsuitable cleaning substances. Routine maintenance is not a warranty repair.

Normal wear from ordinary use is not covered unless it results from defective materials or workmanship. The warranty does not cover the replacement of consumable items simply because they have been used up. A manufacturing fault affecting such an item will still be assessed under the warranty.

Cosmetic damage must be reported within 15 days of delivery. Scratches, dents, marks and changes in appearance caused by handling, cleaning or use after delivery are not covered. This reporting requirement does not remove your statutory rights if goods arrive damaged or do not meet the standard required by law.

Faults caused by alterations, unsuitable replacement parts or repairs carried out incorrectly are excluded. Having work carried out by an independent repairer does not automatically invalidate the warranty. We may decline a claim where that work caused the fault or damage being claimed for.

The warranty does not cover damage caused by use in a business or other setting where the appliance is used outside its stated purpose. Claims will be assessed against the intended use described in the supplied instructions, rather than rejected solely because of where the appliance is located.

An inspection that finds misuse is charged at £65.00. We will explain the inspection arrangements and the circumstances in which this charge applies before you agree to a visit. If we decline a claim because of misuse, we will explain the findings supporting that decision.

The warranty does not provide compensation for inconvenience, loss of use or other indirect losses. However, these exclusions do not limit any liability that Halvard Home cannot lawfully exclude. Your statutory rights remain unaffected, including any right to seek a remedy from the retailer that sold you the goods.

The Brio kettle is covered for 109 months from the date of delivery. This cover applies to faults covered by the warranty and is subject to its terms. The delivery date, rather than the date you register the kettle or start using it, sets the start of the cover.

Keep your order confirmation, delivery record and proof of purchase somewhere safe. These documents help us confirm when your cover began and whether a repair request falls within it. If your records show different delivery dates, contact Halvard Home so that we can check the details with you.

If you cannot find your delivery record, please contact us with the purchase details you have. We will review the available evidence before confirming the start date. Registering your kettle helps us find your information, but registration does not change the delivery date used to calculate your cover.

Replacement parts fitted to the Brio kettle are covered for a further 17 months. This cover starts on the date the replacement part is fitted. It applies to the replacement part itself and does not restart or extend the warranty for the rest of the kettle. Keep the repair record as evidence of the fitting date.

A replacement part may therefore remain covered after the kettle’s original warranty has ended. In that case, cover is limited to the replacement part and remains subject to the warranty terms. A fault elsewhere in the kettle does not become covered simply because a covered replacement part has been fitted.

Repairs to the Brio kettle include labour only for an opening period. Labour for repairs is free for the first 28 months. This labour cover runs from the kettle’s delivery date. After it ends, a covered fault or replacement part may still qualify for support, but labour may be charged. We will explain any proposed charge before you agree to the work.

Arranging a repair does not restart the kettle’s cover. Please report a fault as soon as you notice it and keep the confirmation of your request. We assess whether the fault was reported within the applicable cover, so a delay in arranging an approved repair does not by itself remove that cover.

If the Brio kettle is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 26 days. This requirement runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the original purchase and delivery details. The transfer does not restart the warranty or change its original expiry date.

These cover periods describe the Halvard Home warranty only. They do not limit your statutory rights. If you are unsure whether your kettle, a replacement part or repair labour is still covered, contact us with your delivery and repair records so that we can explain what applies.

If your Brio kettle develops a fault while it is under warranty, contact Halvard Home before arranging a repair. Describe what has happened and have your proof of purchase ready. We may ask about how the kettle has been used and request photographs to help us assess the fault.

Stop using the kettle if it leaks, gives off a burning smell or shows damage to its plug or cable. Unplug it if it is safe to do so. Do not open the casing or try to repair electrical components yourself.

We will explain whether the fault appears to be covered and how to make the kettle available for inspection. If we need you to send it to us, we will provide packing and collection instructions. Let the kettle cool, empty it and make sure it is dry before packing it.

Once we have inspected the kettle, we will confirm whether the repair is covered by the warranty. Covered repairs include the labour, parts and transport we arrange. If we find damage or a fault that is not covered, we will explain our findings and ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work.

A warranty repair to the Brio kettle is completed within 25 weeks of the fault being confirmed. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and keep you informed about the progress of the repair. Please let us know if your contact details change while the kettle is with us.

If a repair to the Brio kettle takes longer than 36 weeks, Halvard Home lends a replacement. The replacement remains our property and is provided for use while your kettle is being repaired. We will explain how it will reach you and arrange its return when your repaired kettle is available.

We may use new or refurbished parts where they are suitable for the repair. Refurbished parts are checked before use to make sure they meet our safety and performance requirements. A refurbished part is covered for 52 weeks. We will identify any refurbished part fitted and explain how to report a fault with it.

Before returning your kettle, we will check that the repair has addressed the confirmed fault and that the kettle operates safely. We will also provide a summary of the work carried out. If the same problem continues, contact us so that we can review the repair.

An engineer visit for the Brio kettle after the warranty has ended costs £105.00. We will explain what the visit includes and whether any separate repair charges would apply before you agree to an appointment.

Nothing in this repair process limits your statutory rights. You may also have rights against the retailer that sold you the kettle, regardless of whether a fault is covered by this warranty.

The Tessa dishwasher is covered for 104 months from the date of delivery. The delivery date is the date the appliance arrives at the address given for your order, rather than the date you place the order or arrange installation. Please keep your delivery confirmation with your proof of purchase.

If your paperwork shows a different delivery date from the date you received your Tessa dishwasher, contact Halvard Home so we can check the record. We may ask for evidence from you or the delivery company. Correcting a delivery record does not change the cover you are entitled to receive.

Your warranty starts from delivery even if you choose to leave the appliance unpacked or delay using it. Installation, registration and use do not reset the start date. Registering your details helps us deal with a claim, but the delivery record is what establishes when your cover begins.

Replacement parts fitted to the Tessa dishwasher are covered for a further 74 months. This cover starts on the date the replacement part is fitted under the warranty. Keep the repair record, as it identifies the part and confirms the fitting date used to assess a claim relating to it.

The cover for a replacement part applies to that part, rather than restarting the warranty for the appliance. If you contact us about a replacement part, please explain the fault and provide the repair record if you have it. We can also check our service records to help establish its cover.

Labour for repairs to the Tessa dishwasher is free for the first 48 months. This applies to repairs accepted under the warranty and carried out through Halvard Home’s authorised service arrangements. Please contact us before arranging a repair yourself, as work arranged independently is not automatically covered.

After the free labour cover ends, a covered part may still qualify for replacement, but fitting it may involve a labour charge. We will explain the applicable charge and ask for your agreement before arranging chargeable work. Cover for a replacement part does not restart the appliance’s free labour cover.

The warranty on the Tessa dishwasher can pass to a new owner. If it is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 34 days. To arrange the transfer, the new owner should contact Halvard Home with proof of the sale and the appliance’s delivery and warranty records.

A change of ownership does not restart the appliance’s cover or alter the fitting date recorded for a covered replacement part. The new owner takes over the cover that remains available under this policy. We will confirm the transfer and explain the cover shown in our records.

If you are unsure whether your Tessa dishwasher or a replacement part is still covered, contact us before booking a repair. We will use the delivery details and relevant repair records to check. This warranty is separate from your legal rights and does not limit your rights against the seller.

If your Tessa dishwasher develops a fault covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Please have your proof of purchase ready and describe what has gone wrong. We may ask for photographs or information from the appliance label to help identify the fault.

Our support team will explain whether the fault can be assessed remotely or needs an engineer’s visit. Please do not attempt a repair yourself. If the dishwasher is leaking, smells of burning or appears unsafe, stop using it and follow the safety guidance in its instruction booklet.

We will confirm whether the fault is covered before authorising repair work. Repairs under warranty include the labour and parts needed to correct the covered fault, without charge. If the assessment identifies work outside the warranty, we will explain the reason and seek your agreement before proceeding.

For repairs that can be carried out through our standard service using available parts, our completion commitment is as follows. A warranty repair to the Tessa dishwasher is completed within 21 weeks of the fault being confirmed.

An exception applies where the repair depends on parts that must be specially sourced. Some repairs to the Tessa dishwasher need parts that are not held in stock. If a repair takes longer than 40 weeks, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

We will explain how the loan arrangement works and agree delivery and collection with you. The replacement is provided for your household’s use and remains Halvard Home’s property. Please take reasonable care of it and tell us if it develops a fault or is damaged.

Please make the Tessa dishwasher accessible for the engineer and remove items that could obstruct the work. Tell us about access restrictions or installation features that may affect the repair. Our team will discuss suitable arrangements with you rather than asking you to move an appliance unsafely.

A repair may use a new or refurbished part that meets our safety and performance requirements. We will tell you if a refurbished part is fitted and record this in the repair paperwork. A refurbished part is covered for 73 weeks.

The engineer will check the repair and explain the work carried out. Please keep the repair record with your proof of purchase. If the reported fault remains, or you believe the repair has caused a problem, contact us so that we can review the work.

We will keep you informed about parts availability and changes affecting the repair. If you are unhappy with how your claim has been handled, ask our support team to review it through our complaints process. Repairs under this warranty do not affect your statutory rights.

The Orrin heat pump is covered for 114 months from the date of delivery. The delivery date, rather than the date you ordered, paid for or started using it, determines when the warranty begins. Keep your delivery confirmation with your proof of purchase so that we can check when your cover started.

The warranty covers faults in the Orrin heat pump that arise from defects in materials or manufacture, subject to the conditions and exclusions in this policy. It does not cover every problem that may affect the appliance. Whether a repair qualifies depends on the cause of the fault as well as whether the warranty is still active.

Labour for repairs to the Orrin heat pump is free for the first 11 months. This applies to labour needed to carry out a repair accepted under the warranty. It does not make unrelated work, routine servicing or repairs outside the warranty free of charge.

When the free labour cover ends, qualifying replacement parts remain covered while the warranty is active, but you will need to pay for repair labour. We will explain any proposed charges before arranging chargeable work. You can then decide whether you wish to proceed.

If you are unsure whether your cover is active, contact Halvard Home with your purchase and delivery records. If those records are missing or show conflicting information, we may ask for supporting evidence. We will explain what information is needed to confirm the delivery date.

Please tell us about a fault while the warranty is active. We will use the date you report it when checking whether it falls within the cover period. A delay in arranging an approved repair will not, by itself, make an otherwise valid claim fall outside the warranty.

Repairing the Orrin heat pump or fitting a replacement part does not restart or extend its warranty. Work accepted under the warranty remains linked to the original delivery date. Keep the repair record with your purchase documents so that the history of the appliance is available if needed.

If the Orrin heat pump is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 24 days. The transfer deadline is measured from the date of sale. The seller should pass the purchase, delivery and repair records to the new owner, who should contact Halvard Home to arrange the transfer.

A transfer changes the registered owner but does not restart the cover or restore free labour cover that has ended. The new owner receives the cover that is still active, subject to the same warranty conditions and exclusions.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights as a consumer. Its expiry, or the end of free labour cover, does not remove rights you may have under consumer law against the seller.

If your Orrin heat pump develops a fault while its warranty is valid, contact Halvard Home to request a repair. Tell us what has happened, how the fault affects the heating or hot water, and whether you have noticed any unusual sounds, smells or leaks. Please have your proof of purchase available so that we can check your warranty cover.

We will ask about the fault and explain whether there are any safe checks you can carry out. You do not need to open the casing or attempt a repair yourself. If you think the appliance is unsafe, stop using it and contact us for advice. Do not touch exposed wiring or leaking components.

We will arrange an engineer visit if the fault cannot be assessed or resolved remotely. Please make sure the engineer can reach the appliance safely and that the surrounding area is clear. Let us know about access restrictions or any support you need when arranging the appointment.

The engineer will assess the appliance and explain what needs to be repaired. We will confirm whether the fault is covered by the warranty before carrying out work. Repairs covered by the warranty include the necessary parts, labour and engineer travel, without a repair charge to you.

A warranty repair to the Orrin heat pump is completed within 37 weeks of the fault being confirmed.

We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and keep you informed about the repair arrangements. If parts need to be ordered or an appointment needs to change, we will explain what this means for your repair. Please tell us if your contact details change so that we can keep you updated.

If a repair takes longer than 5 weeks, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

We will discuss the replacement arrangements with you, including delivery, safe use and collection. The replacement remains the property of Halvard Home. Please follow the instructions supplied with it and contact us if it develops a fault. We will explain how to return it when your repaired appliance is ready to use.

The engineer will check the repaired appliance and explain the work carried out. We will also provide a record of the repair. Keep this with your warranty documents and contact us if the fault returns or the appliance does not work as expected.

If the assessment shows that the fault is not covered, we will explain why and provide details of any proposed charges. We will ask for your agreement before carrying out chargeable work. You can ask us to review a decision if you believe we have misunderstood the fault or your warranty cover.

An engineer visit for the Orrin heat pump after the warranty has ended costs £57.00.

We will explain any separate repair costs before you agree to proceed. Nothing in this section limits your statutory rights, including rights you may have against the seller. Warranty support is provided in addition to those rights.

If your Lumen smart thermostat develops a fault during its warranty, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Tell us what is happening and have your proof of purchase available. We may ask for details about the installation and any messages shown on the display so that we can understand the problem and advise you safely.

We will explain whether the fault can be assessed remotely or needs an engineer visit. Please do not remove the thermostat from its mounting or attempt electrical work yourself. If you notice overheating, a burning smell or exposed wiring, stop using the thermostat and seek advice from a qualified electrician.

Before arranging a repair, we will check that the fault is covered by the warranty. Cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship. Damage caused by misuse, unsuitable installation or unauthorised alterations is not covered. We will explain our decision and tell you if we need further information.

Where the fault is covered, Halvard Home pays for the necessary assessment, labour and parts. We will not carry out chargeable work without explaining the cost and obtaining your agreement. If the assessment finds damage outside the warranty, you can decide whether to accept a paid repair.

A warranty repair to the Lumen smart thermostat is completed within 10 weeks of the fault being confirmed. We will tell you when the fault has been confirmed and explain how the repair will be arranged. Please make sure we have your current contact details so that we can keep you informed.

If a repair takes longer than 30 weeks, Halvard Home lends a replacement. The loan remains Halvard Home’s property. We will explain the delivery, installation and return arrangements, including how to look after it while your thermostat is being repaired. There is no charge for the loan.

An engineer visit for the Lumen smart thermostat after the warranty has ended costs £110.00. This charge does not apply to a visit needed to complete an accepted warranty repair. For work outside the warranty, we will explain what the visit charge includes and whether parts or further work would cost extra.

We may use new or refurbished parts where suitable. Refurbished parts are checked for safety, condition and compatibility before fitting. A refurbished part fitted to the Lumen smart thermostat is covered for 79 weeks. This cover begins when the part is fitted and applies to faults in that part.

Please provide safe access for the engineer and tell us about anything that could affect the visit. You should also let us know about any accessibility needs when booking, so that we can discuss suitable arrangements.

After the repair, we will explain what work was carried out and whether any settings need your attention. Keep the repair record with your proof of purchase. If the fault returns, contact us with those details. Your warranty cover is separate from, and does not limit, your statutory rights.

The Lumen smart thermostat is covered for 101 months from the date of delivery. Your delivery date is the date the thermostat arrives at the address given in your order, rather than the date you buy it or arrange installation. Installing or activating it later does not change when the warranty starts.

Keep your order confirmation and proof of delivery somewhere safe. These records help us confirm whether your thermostat is still covered when you contact us. If you cannot find them, please get in touch with Halvard Home. We will check the records available to us and explain whether we need anything else.

Labour for repairs to the Lumen smart thermostat is free for the first 27 months. This applies to work authorised by Halvard Home for a fault covered by the warranty. Please contact us before arranging a repair yourself, as we cannot promise to pay for work that we have not approved.

After the free labour cover ends, charges for repair work may apply even if the thermostat remains under warranty. Parts needed to put right a covered fault remain covered until the warranty ends. We will explain any labour charges before you agree to the work, so you can decide whether to proceed.

If the Lumen smart thermostat is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 94 days. This deadline runs from the date of the sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home to request the transfer and provide evidence of the sale, together with the original delivery details where available.

A transfer carries over the cover that remains; it does not restart the warranty or renew free labour cover. The original delivery date continues to determine when cover ends. If the transfer deadline is missed, the new owner cannot claim under this warranty. Please keep written confirmation of a completed transfer.

An authorised repair or replacement does not restart or extend the warranty. A replacement supplied under this warranty takes over the cover remaining on the original thermostat. Keep any repair or replacement paperwork with your purchase records so that we can trace the warranty if you need further help.

Please report a fault as soon as you notice it. When you contact us, describe what has happened and provide your delivery details if you have them. If you report a covered fault while the warranty is active, the expiry of the warranty during our assessment will not, by itself, prevent that claim from being considered.

The cover described here is Halvard Home’s warranty and is separate from your legal rights. Those rights are not reduced when free labour cover ends or when the warranty expires. You may still have a right to a remedy from the seller under applicable consumer law.

The Keel washing machine is covered for 98 months from the date of delivery. Your delivery record is the starting point for working out when this cover ends. Keep your order confirmation and proof of delivery somewhere safe, as we may ask to see them when you make a claim.

If your receipt shows a purchase date that differs from the delivery date, we use the delivery date. If you cannot find your delivery record, contact Halvard Home. We will check the information available to us and explain what other evidence we can accept to confirm when your cover began.

The warranty applies to faults covered by its terms that arise during the applicable cover period. Contact us when you notice a fault, and describe what has happened. We will explain whether the issue falls within the warranty and what you need to do next. Do not arrange a repair at our expense without our agreement.

Replacement parts fitted to the Keel washing machine are covered for a further 76 months. This cover starts on the date the replacement part is fitted under an approved warranty repair. Keep the repair confirmation, as it identifies the part and records the fitting date used to establish its cover.

Replacement part cover applies to the fitted part, rather than renewing the warranty for the whole appliance. It does not change the cover end date for unrelated components. If you believe a replacement part has developed a fault, contact us with the repair details so we can check the applicable cover.

Labour for repairs is free for the first 31 months. This applies to work approved by Halvard Home to put right a fault covered by the warranty. The labour cover starts from the delivery date of the appliance, rather than from the date you register it or report a fault.

Outside that labour cover, you may need to pay for repair work even if the faulty part remains covered. We will explain any proposed labour charge before you agree to the repair. Having a replacement part fitted does not restart the appliance’s free labour cover.

If the Keel washing machine is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 83 days. This transfer deadline runs from the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the available delivery and repair records.

Transferring the warranty does not restart or extend its cover. We use the original delivery record and any approved replacement part records to establish which cover still applies. We will confirm the transfer and explain any information that is missing.

These warranty terms do not affect your statutory rights. If you are unsure whether your appliance, a replacement part or repair labour is still covered, contact Halvard Home before agreeing to paid work.

If your Keel washing machine develops a fault covered by its warranty, contact Halvard Home to arrange an assessment. Have your proof of purchase and a description of the problem ready. Tell us about any warning shown on the display, unusual noise or leak, without attempting to take the machine apart.

We will explain how the fault will be assessed and whether an engineer needs to visit your home. You may be asked to carry out simple checks that are safe to do yourself. Do not continue using the machine if you suspect it is unsafe. Tell us if you cannot safely disconnect it.

Once we have confirmed that the fault is covered, we will arrange the repair and explain what happens next. Covered repairs include the labour and parts needed to put the fault right. We will not ask you to pay for covered work or proceed with chargeable work without your agreement.

A warranty repair to the Keel washing machine is completed within 20 weeks of the fault being confirmed. We will keep you informed about the repair arrangements and contact you if access, parts availability or another issue affects the work. Please tell us if your contact details change.

If a repair to the Keel washing machine takes longer than 34 weeks, Halvard Home lends a replacement. We will contact you to arrange delivery and explain how to use and care for the loan machine. It remains the property of Halvard Home, and we will arrange its collection when it is no longer needed.

Please make sure the engineer can reach the machine safely. Clear the surrounding area and let us know about stairs, restricted access or anything else that could affect the visit. If you cannot attend the agreed appointment, contact us so that we can rearrange it.

We may use a new or refurbished part where suitable. Any refurbished part will be checked for safety and suitability before it is fitted. A refurbished part fitted to the Keel washing machine is covered for 11 weeks. Contact us if you believe a fitted part has developed a fault.

An engineer visit for the Keel washing machine after the warranty has ended costs £56.00. We will explain any separate charges for parts or repair work before you decide whether to proceed. Paying for a visit does not commit you to accepting a repair quotation.

If our assessment finds that the fault is not covered, we will explain the reason and discuss the available options. You can ask us to review the decision if you think relevant information has been missed. Nothing in this warranty limits your statutory rights, including rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the machine.

The Ashby tumble dryer is covered for 142 months from the date of delivery. Your cover begins when the appliance is delivered to you, rather than when you place your order, make payment or begin using it.

Keep your delivery confirmation with your proof of purchase. These documents help us confirm when your cover began and whether a fault falls within the warranty. If your records show different delivery dates, contact Halvard Home so that we can check them with you.

If you cannot find your delivery confirmation, please contact us with the purchase details you have available. We will help you look for evidence of delivery. Do not assume that missing paperwork means your warranty has ended or that you cannot ask for help.

Replacement parts fitted to the Ashby tumble dryer are covered for a further 80 months. This cover begins on the date the replacement part is fitted under the warranty. Keep the repair record, as it identifies the part and confirms when its cover began.

The cover for a replacement part applies to that part, rather than restarting the warranty for the appliance as a whole. A replacement part may therefore remain covered after the appliance warranty has ended. Contact us if you need help checking which cover applies to a fault.

Labour for repairs to the Ashby tumble dryer is free for the first 47 months. This applies to repairs accepted under the warranty. The delivery date is used to establish whether the free labour cover applies when you report the fault.

After the free labour cover has ended, a labour charge may apply even where the appliance or a replacement part remains covered. We will explain any proposed charge before arranging chargeable work. You can then decide whether you wish to proceed.

If the Ashby tumble dryer is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 91 days. This transfer window begins on the date of sale. The new owner should contact Halvard Home with evidence of the sale and the available purchase, delivery and repair records.

Transferring the warranty does not restart the appliance cover, replacement part cover or free labour cover. The new owner receives the cover that remains available under the existing warranty, subject to its terms. We will confirm the relevant cover details when the transfer is completed.

Please report a fault as soon as you notice it and keep a copy of your message or service reference. We use the date you report the fault to assess whether the relevant cover is still active. An appointment arranged for after that cover ends does not, by itself, make an accepted claim invalid.

This warranty is separate from your legal rights. Its cover limits do not remove or restrict the rights you may have against the seller under consumer law.

If your Ashby tumble dryer develops a fault covered by the warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair through an authorised engineer. The warranty covers the parts and labour needed to put right faults caused by defective materials or workmanship, subject to the warranty terms.
